newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco wheat imports fall to 2.24 mln T in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco wheat imports fall to 2.24 mln T in 1996.

text.p: Morocco imported 2.24 million tonnes of wheat in calendar 1996 worth 4.13 billion dirhams ($435 million), the state-run Office des Changes said on Tuesday.
In a monthly newsletter, the regulatory body said this compared with 2.54 million tonnes worth 3.99 billion dirhams ($420 million) in 1995.
It gave no breakdown of soft and hard wheat tonnage. According to agriculture ministry estimates, soft wheat imports in second half 1996 reached 690,000 tonnes and hard wheat 206,000 tonnes.

Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals in the 1995/96 agricultural season (which runs for 12 months from around end-May/June) against only 1.6 million tonnes in 1994/95, when agriculture was hit by serious drought.
Morocco's maize imports remained static at 0.54 million tonnes in 1996, the Office des Changes said. But they slightly rose in value to 893 million dirhams against 707 million in 1995.
Barley imports in 1996 dropped to 29,684 tonnes, costing 48.4 million dirhams, from 465,028 tonnes at a cost of 536.1 million dirhams in 1995, it said.
Last month, Finance Minister Mohammed Kabbaj said Morocco expected a serious decline in cereal output to between 3.5 and 4.0 million tonnes this year due to the weather.
The impact of this was expected put the economy into zero growth in 1997 compared with positive growth of 11.8 percent in gross domestic product last year, the ministry said.
Agriculture represents around 20 percent of GDP and employs nearly half of the country's 10 million workforce.
